problem: Visual-trajectory-following methods based on image prediction/visual MPC have short predictive horizons and blurry long-horizon predictions, so they fail to deviate around large unseen obstacles that occlude the next subgoal. Deterministic imitation also ignores the multimodality of human teleoperation.
motivation: Humans follow a sequence of images robustly despite environment changes and obstacles by mentally simulating future views. Robots with only an RGB camera need a long-horizon yet accurate predictive mechanism plus diverse avoidance strategies, without a metric map. The observation is that the subgoal image itself can serve as the far end of a prediction, as in bidirectional search.
key_idea: Predict future images bidirectionally (forward from the current image and backward from the subgoal image) conditioned on sampled velocity sequences learned probabilistically from teleoperator demos, and choose the sample that is reachable and traversable.
insight: Backward prediction from the subgoal doubles the horizon (2L) without extra image degradation. Baselines drop when the horizon goes from 8 to 16 (DVMPC SR 0.700 to 0.469), while the full method at 16 reaches 0.807. Ablations show each component helps: removing probabilistic control costs the most (0.731), then removing bidirectional prediction (0.777) and subgoal selection (0.787).
method: Subgoal selection (SS): uses the virtual velocities from the CP module to compute the pose of each subgoal in the robot frame, picks the furthest of the N subgoals within thresholds d_th=0.8 m and theta_th=0.4 rad, and avoids comparing against every subgoal image.

Control policy (CP): N weight-shared recurrent LSTM units, one per upcoming subgoal image, each outputting a Gaussian over (v, w) for 2L steps; M sampled velocity sequences per unit (N=M=3 at inference, mean and ±2 sigma on angular velocity).

Bidirectional image loss: VUNet-360 predicts L forward images from I_t with u_0..L-1 and L backward images from subgoal I_{s+i} with reversed, negated velocities; the two predictions are forced to match at the midpoint step L (w_L=5).

Trajectory likelihood + smoothness loss: NLL of the teleoperator trajectory under the odometry-propagated Gaussian (covariance from the Jacobian) plus an MSE smoothness term; total J = J_bimg + 0.001 J_tl + 1.0 J_smo.

Trajectory selection (TS): scores S = reachability (learned triplet-loss feature distance between forward and backward mid-images) + traversability (GONet on the predicted front image; penalty 100 if p<0.5); overrides with a 90° pivot if the current view is untraversable.
Training data: GO Stanford 4 (10.3 h real TurtleBot2 360° camera data plus 3.6 h Gibson simulation), 128x128 images.

setting.backbone: CNN + LSTM control policy, pretrained VUNet-360 image predictor, GONet traversability net, CNN f_ev (all trained)
setting.training_data: GO Stanford 4: 10.3 h real teleoperation (12 buildings) + 3.6 h Gibson simulator teleoperation (36 buildings), mixed
setting.observation: 360° RGB fisheye camera (front+back images concatenated in channels), 128x128
setting.action_space: continuous linear/angular velocity (v max 0.5 m/s, w max 1.0 rad/s; inference v limited to 0.2 m/s), with 90° pivot override
setting.privileged: none (a prerecorded visual trajectory of subgoal images is given as the task specification)

numbers_note: Results are on a custom benchmark, not standard ones. Obstacle-scale and distance results appear only in figures. Different-robot test: 80% success over 10 trials in 2 environments (text only).
results: On simulated visual-trajectory following with unseen obstacles, the full method gets 0.807 goal arrival rate, 0.905 subgoal coverage and 0.803 SPL, beating the strongest baseline DVMPC (8 steps, 0.700/0.850/0.700). In real-world tests, goal arrival is 0.8-0.9 versus 0.5-0.6 for DVMPC. It also reaches the goal in 80% of trials on an unseen robot embodiment.
limitations: GONet traversability occasionally mispredicts, causing collisions, and it fails on suddenly appearing dynamic obstacles.
Loses localization when the robot is kidnapped, so the SS module fails; it needs global mapping/planning.
Runs at only ~5.3 Hz, with N=M=3 samples and limited velocity at inference.
compares_to: Stochastic optimization / CEM visual MPC (Finn et al.)
